In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Fourier–Deligne transform''', or '''ℓ-adic Fourier transform''', or '''geometric Fourier transform''', is an operation on objects of the [[derived category]] of [[l-adic sheaf|''ℓ''-adic sheaves]] over the affine line. It was introduced by [[Pierre Deligne]] on November 29, 1976 in a letter  to  [[David Kazhdan]]  as an analogue of the usual [[Fourier transform]]. It was used by [[Gérard Laumon]] to simplify Deligne's proof of the [[Weil conjectures]].
